prerequisites: It is recommended to have completed the course Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering.

learning_outcomes.text: Properly use basic laboratory instrumentation: signal generator, oscilloscope and multimeter.
Properly use electronic circuit simulators, and take advantage of them for self-learning.
Know the most common circuits with diodes, bipolar junction transistors, field effect transistors, operational amplifiers and logic circuits.
Manage information coding and Boolean algebra to design and electronically implement logic functions.
Explain the functionality of common digital blocks and know how to combine and use them.
Apply state graphs to the description of sequential electronic circuits and solve them in terms of Boolean functions.

syllabus_topics: Digital electronic systems and/or operational amplifiers.
teaching_methods: Theoretical classes, using audiovisual media and technological resources to explain basic aspects of the syllabus.
Practical classes in the classroom, focusing on problem-solving related to theoretical content, including complementary problems for self-learning.
Laboratory practical classes in groups, focusing on case-based or practical exercises for designing and implementing circuits.
Preparation of reports and/or project memories based on solving problems or practical cases through simulation, proposed by the professor.
Tutorials (three 1-hour sessions) for resolving questions and doubts.

assessment_methods.method: Development test of theory and problems (A)
Development test of theory and problems (B)
Real and/or simulated task execution tests (D)

assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, the final grade is the sum of grades from A (20%), B (50%), C (10%), and D (20%), with a minimum combined score of 3/7 required for tests A and B; otherwise, the final grade is based only on A and B weighted over 10. Students must attend at least 75% of lab practicals (D) to follow continuous assessment. For single assessment, a development test (A, 60%) and a lab task execution test (B, 40%) are given; a minimum of 3/6 on A is required to take B, and a minimum of 2/4 on B is needed to sum A and B, otherwise the final grade is based on A or the average of A and B. In the second call, continuous assessment grades A, C, and D are retained, and tests A and B can be retaken.
